faqs.question: Which is better, Nothing Ear (a) or CMF Buds Pro 2?
faqs.answer: Choose according to priorities. Nothing Ear (a) offers a compact Nothing-branded design, 45dB ANC and strong battery claims; CMF Buds Pro 2 adds dual drivers, Smart Dial and up-to-50dB theoretical ANC. Fit, price and phone compatibility decide the better purchase.

faqs.question: Which has stronger ANC?
faqs.answer: CMF Buds Pro 2 advertises hybrid ANC up to a theoretical 50dB, while Nothing Ear (a) advertises up to 45dB. These are laboratory maximums; seal, ear tips and sound environment matter more in daily use.

faqs.question: Do both support LDAC?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both products support LDAC alongside AAC and SBC, but the source device must support LDAC. iPhone users should not expect LDAC through standard iOS Bluetooth audio.

faqs.question: Which has better sound hardware?
faqs.answer: CMF Buds Pro 2 uses an 11mm driver plus a 6mm micro-planar tweeter, while Ear (a) uses an 11mm dynamic driver. Driver count does not determine personal preference; tuning and fit remain important.

faqs.question: Which has better battery life?
faqs.answer: Official laboratory claims list Ear (a) at up to 42.5 hours with its case and ANC off, while CMF Buds Pro 2 lists up to 43 hours under specified conditions. ANC, codec, volume and calls reduce both results.

faqs.question: Does Ear (a) have a Smart Dial?
faqs.answer: No. CMF Buds Pro 2 has the rotating and press-based Smart Dial on its charging case. Ear (a) uses customisable pinch controls and Nothing X settings.

faqs.question: Which is better for calls?
faqs.answer: Both use microphone noise-reduction features. CMF Buds Pro 2 lists six microphones, while Ear (a) uses three per earbud. Real call quality depends on wind, fit, app processing and the phone connection.

faqs.question: Which is better for gaming?
faqs.answer: Both support a low-lag mode that can reduce latency when paired with Nothing phones under stated conditions. Game audio, Bluetooth conditions and total device latency still matter; neither changes game FPS or network ping.

faqs.question: Which is more water resistant?
faqs.answer: CMF Buds Pro 2 earbuds are rated IP55 and Ear (a) earbuds IP54 under controlled tests. Neither charging case is intended to be waterproof, and neither product is for swimming or showering.

faqs.question: Which is more comfortable?
faqs.answer: Comfort is individual. Earbud shape, tip seal, weight and ear anatomy matter more than brand. Try all supplied tip sizes and test walking, speaking and longer listening before deciding.

faqs.question: Which should I buy for a Nothing Phone?
faqs.answer: Both integrate with Nothing X and support useful Nothing-phone features. Pick Ear (a) for its compact Nothing identity or CMF Buds Pro 2 for Smart Dial, dual drivers and its broader control set.
